questions.stem: An engineer's design brief sets a token bucket of capacity 10 refilling at 2 tokens per second; explain how many requests a burst of 14 can send immediately and what happens to the rest.

questions.explanation: Capacity caps the instant burst while the refill rate governs sustained throughput. Excess requests queue or are rejected depending on policy.

options.text: 1, assuming only one refill per window
8, adding refill to capacity
3, forgetting the initial tokens
5, because capacity caps the refill

questions.explanation: The bucket refills to capacity 5 then stops. Three seconds of idle time still leaves 5 tokens, not 8.

questions.topic: One query per row of a result set
questions.stem: An engineer's design brief still runs N+1 queries after adding an index; why did the index not fix it?

options.text: The index is on the wrong column
options.misconception: blames column choice for a shape issue

options.text: The problem is query count, not scan cost
The database ignores indexes in loops
N+1 only happens without caching

questions.explanation: An index speeds each individual query but does not reduce how many queries are issued. Fix the query shape with a join or batch.

questions.subject: WEB_DEVELOPMENT
questions.topic: Paging by offset after a row above the page is deleted
questions.stem: An engineer's design brief needs stable paging under concurrent deletes; explain why keyset pagination beats offset.

answer.exemplar: Keyset pagination anchors each page to the last seen value rather than a count, so deletions above the page do not shift the window. Offset counts from the start and skips rows.

questions.explanation: Keyset uses a cursor on a sorted column, making pages stable under inserts and deletes. Offset is a fragile count.
questions.hint: Anchor to a value, not a count.

Only exact example.com passes

The check throws on unknown hosts

questions.explanation: Substring matching accepts any host containing the trusted string. Use exact equality or a parsed allowlist.

questions.subject: WEB_DEVELOPMENT
questions.topic: Two identical writes from one click
questions.stem: An engineer's design brief adds an idempotency key to a payment request; explain how the server uses it to prevent duplicates.

answer.exemplar: The server stores the result keyed by the client's idempotency key. A retry with the same key returns the stored result instead of charging again.

questions.explanation: The key makes retries safe: the first request executes, later identical keys replay the stored response.
questions.hint: Key ties retry to first result.

questions.topic: What an index changes about the work a lookup does

questions.topic: The stages a service worker passes through
questions.stem: An engineer's design brief ships a new service worker while an old one controls pages; explain how the new worker takes over.

answer.exemplar: The new worker installs and waits. Once all old tabs close or skipWaiting is called, it activates and claims clients, then controls future fetches.

questions.explanation: A waiting worker activates only when no clients are controlled or skipWaiting is invoked. Then it claims clients.
